references.text: The first time the daughters of Zelophehad are mentioned by name: Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah and Tirzah, who had no brothers.
The daughters of Zelophehad come to Moses to claim their inheritance rights, since their father died without sons. The Lord grants them the right to inherit.

Background for the marriage rule: The heads of families in the tribe of Manasseh were concerned that the inheritance would pass to other tribes if the daughters of Zelophehad married outside the tribe.
Moses gives the command that daughters who inherit land must marry within their father's tribe, so that the inheritance remains in the tribe.
During the distribution of land in Joshua's time, the daughters of Zelophehad receive their share in the tribe of Manasseh, as the Lord had commanded through Moses.
The genealogy mentions Zelophehad as the son of Hepher and confirms that he had only daughters.
